blocks.content: Table 6-4. Rx Data Interface Output Signals

|  Name | Active Level | Description | Relevant Protocols  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  Original PIPE: RxData[31:0] for 32-bit interface RxData[15:0] for 16-bit interface or RxData[7:0] for 8-bit interface SerDes arch: RxData[159:0] RxData[79:0] for 80-bit interface RxData[39:0] for 40-bit interface RxData[19:0] for 20-bit interface or RxData[9:0] for 10-bit interface Serdes arch (USB4 only): RxData[55:0] for 56-bit interface | N/A | Parallel data output bus for Rx diff pair. For the 16-bit interface, 16 bits represent two symbols of Rx data. Bits [7:0] are the first symbol received, and bits [15:8] are the second symbol. For the 32-bit interface, 32 bits represent the four symbols of Rx data. Bits [23:16] are the third symbol received, and bits [31:24] are the fourth symbol received. Bit zero is the first bit received. When the PHY is in SATA mode, the first valid data following an ALIGN primitive must appear as byte zero in the Rx data. For the SerDes architecture, the RxData signal width options are 160, 80, 40, 20, and 10 bits. For the 80-bit interface, 80 bits represent eight symbols of Rx data. Bits [49:40], bits [59:50], bits [69:60], and bits [79:70] are the fifth, sixth, seventh, and eighth symbols, respectively. For the 160-bit interface, 160 bits represent 16 symbols of Rx data. Bits [89:80], bits [99:90], bits [109:100], bits [119:110], bits [129:120], bits [139:130], bits [149:140], bits [159:150] are the ninth, tenth, eleventh, twelfth, thirteenth, fourteenth, fifteenth, and sixteenth symbols, respectively. For block-encoded data^{1}, only 8 bits out of each 10-bit slice are used, for example, [7:0] represent byte0, [9:8] are reserved, [17:10] represent byte1, and [19:18] are reserved, and so forth. Bit zero is the first bit received. Additionally for SerDes architecture, USB4 uses a 56-bit interface instead of an 80-bit interface. Refer to Section 8.34.3 for details of the 56-bit interface. RxData is synchronous to RxCLK in the SerDes mode. | PCIe, SATA, USB, DisplayPort Rx, USB4  |
|  SerDes arch: RxData2[55:0] for 56-bit interface, RxData2[39:0] for 40-bit interface, RxData2[19:0] for 20-bit interface, or RxData2[9:0] for 10-bit interface | N/A | Parallel data output bus for Rx2 diff pair. For SerDes architecture, the RxData signal width options are 56, 40, 20, and 10 bits. For the 40-bit interface, 40 bits represent 4 symbols of receive data. Bits [9:0], bits [19:10], bits [29:20], and bits[39:30] represent the first, second, third, and fourth symbols, respectively. Refer to Section 8.34.3 for details of the 56-bit interface. RxData2 is synchronous to RxCLK2 in SerDes mode. | DisplayPort RX, USB4  |
